subject: DPA: requested timeline for certified erase + backup carveouts
messages:
From: Emma Chen <emma.chen@acmehealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: dpo@acmehealth.com, vendorops@acmehealth.com
Date: 2028-07-22 08:14 -0700
Subject: DPA redline: certified erasure timing for backups and caches

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the DPA draft. A couple of items our privacy team needs clarified before we can sign:

1) Certified erasure: we need a committed maximum window for certified deletion of customer production data after a deletion request (including primary, KV caches, and any hot prefix caches). The redline currently says "reasonable efforts" which isn't sufficient.

2) Backups and snapshots: are there scope or timing exceptions for cross-region backups and cold snapshots? If so, what are the operational controls and maximum retention windows for backups subject to erasure?

3) Proof of erasure: can you provide an evidence workflow or certificate for completed erasures (for audit)? A one-line confirmation will not be accepted by our auditors.

Please see the attached DPA_redline_v3.docx with comments in the deletion section. Can you and your ops team propose concrete timelines and an evidence template?

Thanks — we'll need this by EOD Tuesday to keep our procurement timeline.

— Emma
Legal Counsel, Acme Health

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Chen <emma.chen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-22 09:42 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redline: certified erasure timing for backups and caches

Emma — thanks for the clear notes and the redline. Appreciate the deadline. High level answers below; I followed with operational detail from Karthik and a proposed evidence template attached.

Summary (TL;DR)
- Certified erasure: 30 calendar days for primary data and live caches; 90 calendar days for backups and cold snapshots in default configuration.
- Cross-region backup exception: backups to other regions can be retained up to 90 days unless customer requests immediate delete; we can offer a 30-day backup SLA for an onshore-only plan as an add-on.
- Proof of erasure: we will provide a signed erase certificate with timestamps, list of systems affected, and a hash of the deleted data objects where available. See attached erase-playbook-summary.pdf.

I'll quote Karthik below for the technical constraints and a mapping of where each type of data lives. If any of these timelines are unacceptable we can propose an onshore-only (private) deployment alternative with tighter windows.

Next steps we propose:
- We accept a 30-day primary/caches / 90-day backup default; include an optional addendum for a 30-day backup SLA (priceable).
- Finalize the erase-certificate format (attached) and include it as an appendix to the DPA.

I'll loop in Pricing/Account to produce an addendum proposal if you prefer the 30-day backup SLA.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference

--- attachment: erase-playbook-summary.pdf (operational playbook excerpt)

On Jul 22, 2028, at 09:03, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai wrote:
> From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
> To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
> Date: 2028-07-22 09:03 -0700
> Subject: RE: tech mapping for erase windows
>
> Kimberly / Laura — quick mapping:
> - Primary request deletion: we can invalidate and purge user-level objects and KV caches within 24 hours; however, continuous-inflight shards and long-lived async queues may hold pointers; full cryptographic wipe at the storage layer completes within 30 days in standard flow.
> - KV/prefix caches: invalidation immediate, on-disk tombstone removal follows standard GC; we commit to visibility of deletion within 24 hours and complete removal within 30 days.
> - Backups/snapshots: incremental snapshots are immutable. Standard retention is 90 days; to meet a 30-day backup SLA we'd need dedicated onshore snapshot lifecycle or contractual snapshot pruning with a paid commitment.
> - Evidence: we can emit a signed manifest that includes timestamps, storage identifiers, and the operator runbook id.
>
> Ops caveat: we cannot guarantee the physical destruction of third-party replicated copies (e.g., cloud provider internal replicas) faster than provider-defined retention; we will include provider acknowledgements in the evidence packet.
>
> Karthik
> Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Emma Chen <emma.chen@acmehealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: dpo@acmehealth.com, vendorops@acmehealth.com
Date: 2028-07-22 12:11 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redline: certified erasure timing for backups and caches

Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick response. A few follow-ups from our DPO:

- 30 days for primary/caches is acceptable if the evidence includes a signed manifest and the actual storage identifiers.
- For backups: 90 days is a bit long for PHI. Our minimum requirement for health data is 45 days for cold snapshots. Can Redwood confirm a pathway to 45 days without an onshore-only commitment? If not, please state that in the DPA and we'll evaluate the add-on.
- Provider replicas: we need the contractual confirmation that Redwood will request deletion from cloud provider replicas and include provider responses in the evidence packet.

Also — auditors require a sample erase certificate. Can you send a filled example (redact customer identifiers) showing the fields you mentioned?

Emma

Subject: Re: DPA redline: certified erasure timing for backups and caches — provider replica confirmation

Emma — technical clarifications: we can implement a 45-day backup window for PHI by changing snapshot lifecycle settings and adding a weekly snapshot-prune job that targets accounts with PHI flags. Operational notes:

- Implementation plan:
  - Week 0: enable PHI flag and snapshot-tagging for Acme tenant.
  - Week 1: deploy prune job to identify and delete incremental snapshots older than 45 days for flagged tenants.
  - Week 2: run two audit-prune cycles and provide the first evidence packet.

- Provider replicas: we will issue scripted deletion requests to the cloud provider's retention team and track response IDs. We cannot force immediate provider-side physical destruction but will include provider response and their internal deletion ticket ids in the evidence.

- Cost/commitment: the 45-day snapshot prune incurs a runbook maintenance and monitoring fee. Pricing will be handled by Account — happy to coordinate.

Karthik

We will insert the provider replica acknowledgement clause and the evidence appendix as discussed.

2) Evidence packet: attached is an example erase certificate (erase-playbook-summary.pdf). We'll provide a redacted sample with real field values for your auditors by EOD Jul 25.

3) Implementation: Karthik will lead the PHI snapshot-prune rollout with a targeted timeline to produce the first audit packet in 2 weeks after agreement.

4) Commercial: Priyom will reach out with the 45-day backup addendum pricing and SOW.

If this plan is acceptable, can you confirm and we will send a follow-up DPA draft (clean + tracked) with the appendix appended.

Best,
Kimberly
